title: Faster Rates for Federated Variational Inequalities
gist: Apple-affiliated NeurIPS paper (Guanghui Wang, Satyen Kale) closes part of the gap between federated variational-inequality convergence rates and federated convex optimization bounds, via a tighter analysis of Local Extra SGD and a new algorithm, LIPPAX, that mitigates client drift. The page also references a related ICML 2024 Apple work noting federated training can be orders of magnitude slower than centralized training, motivating server-side proxy data for tuning.

insights.claim: Convergence rates for federated optimization of stochastic variational inequalities (VIs) lag significantly behind the state-of-the-art bounds known for federated convex optimization.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: VIs underpin min-max/game-style training (e.g., adversarial objectives), so weaker federated guarantees have limited on-device collaborative training of such models.
insights.quote: a significant gap remains between existing convergence rates and the state-of-the-art bounds known for federated convex optimization
insights.locator: In this paper, we study federated

insights.claim: A refined analysis shows the classical Local Extra SGD algorithm admits tighter convergence guarantees than previously known for general smooth and monotone variational inequalities.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Existing federated algorithms may be more efficient than assumed, reducing the need for new infrastructure to get better results.
insights.quote: the classical Local Extra SGD algorithm admits tighter guarantees under a refined analysis

insights.claim: Local Extra SGD has an inherent limitation that can cause excessive client drift, where local client updates diverge from the global objective in federated training.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Client drift is a core bottleneck for federated learning across heterogeneous devices, a key constraint for privacy-first on-device AI strategies.
insights.quote: we identify an inherent limitation of Local Extra SGD, which can lead to excessive client drift

insights.claim: The proposed Local Inexact Proximal Point Algorithm with Extra Step (LIPPAX) mitigates client drift and achieves improved guarantees in bounded Hessian, bounded operator, and low-variance regimes, with results extended to federated composite variational inequalities.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals continued Apple investment in the theoretical foundations of federated learning, consistent with its on-device/privacy positioning.

insights.claim: A related Apple ICML 2024 work states that federated learning training can be orders of magnitude slower than standard centralized training, severely limiting experimentation and hyperparameter tuning.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The speed penalty is a real cost of privacy-preserving training, favoring players with methods to cut iteration time.
insights.quote: training using federated learning can be orders of magnitude slower than standard centralized training

insights.claim: Server-side proxy data can be used to run training simulations, such as hyperparameter tuning, to speed up federated training pipelines by reducing on-device tuning.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Hybrid server/device workflows are a practical route to making federated on-device AI commercially viable.
insights.quote: Server-side proxy data can be used to run training simulations, for instance for hyperparameter tuning.
